title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Playbook
author: Jordan Kim
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's core people operations practices for: hiring and interviewing, offer and negotiation, new-hire onboarding, ongoing performance and feedback cycles, and manager best practices. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and new managers. Use the checklists, templates, and timelines below to reduce variability and improve candidate and employee experience while retaining compliance and fairness.

Scope

- Applies to all full-time and long-term contract hires across Redwood (hosted API, platform, infra, and GTM teams).
- Excludes executive-level hiring (VP+) and acquisitions; separate process managed by People Ops + Legal + CEO.

Hiring process (high-level)

1. Role intake and approval
   - Manager creates a Role Intake form (HRIS link) with: role purpose, scope, level, compensation band, interview panel recommendations, and hiring timeline.
   - People Ops reviews for budget, level calibration, and equity considerations.
   - Approval required from: hiring manager, hiring manager's manager, and People Ops.

2. Sourcing & screening
   - Recruiter screens for minimum requirements and culture fit using a standardized phone screen template.
   - All candidates must have a documented scorecard before on-site interviews.

3. Interview loop and evaluation
   - Standard interview loop for IC roles: phone screen -> technical assessment (take-home or live) -> on-site/interview loop -> hiring committee review.
   - Standard interview loop for manager roles: phone screen -> leadership interview -> case study -> interview loop -> hiring committee review.

Interview scorecards and rubrics

- Every role must have a role-specific scorecard saved in the role folder. Scorecard sections: core competencies, technical bar, collaboration & communication, problem solving, role-specific skills, cultural contributions, and recommended outcome.
- Use a 1-5 rubric with anchors for each competency. Interviewers must provide: numeric scores, notes (2-5 sentences), and one clear recommendation (hire/no hire/hold).

Sample phone screen template (recruiter)

- 5 min: Introductions and role overview
- 15 min: Candidate background and recent work highlights
- 10 min: Role fit & motivation questions
- 10 min: Logistics (remote policy, compensation band, start date)
- 5 min: Next steps and Q&A

Offer & negotiation

- People Ops drafts offers using the approved compensation band. All offers require People Ops review.
- Standard components: base salary, equity grant (if eligible), target bonus (if applicable), benefits summary, relocation/remote stipends, and start date.
- For counteroffers or negotiations: escalate to Senior People Ops for sign-off when request exceeds 10% of band midpoint or involves sign-on > $25k or equity exceptions.

Onboarding (30/60/90 overview)

Objective: get new hires productive and integrated while establishing clear expectations and career pathways. Use the onboarding tracker in HRIS for all tasks.

Day 0/1 checklist

- Equipment: device, accounts, VPN, Slack, email, calendar invites (buddy, manager 1:1), security training enrollment
- People Ops: benefits enrollment link, payroll form, org chart, role readout
- Manager: first-day welcome message, 30/60/90 plan draft, initial expectations doc

Week 1

- Team orientation and introductions, product overview and architecture walkthrough, access to code repos and internal docs, initial small task or orientation assignment
- Buddy program: assign a peer buddy for the first 90 days (buddy checklist included)

30/60/90 plan (example milestones)

- 30 days: complete training, ship small task, complete codebase walkthrough, meet cross-functional partners
- 60 days: take ownership of a medium-scope task, demonstrate consistent coding/review patterns or team leadership behaviors, initial performance checkpoint with manager
- 90 days: full ownership of core responsibilities, calibration conversation with manager & People Ops, update career development plan

Manager responsibilities for onboarding

- Schedule recurring 1:1s (weekly for first 8 weeks, then biweekly), define explicit first-90 expectations, provide weekly feedback, ensure cross-team introductions, and complete 30/60/90 check-ins in HRIS.

Performance & feedback cycles

Cadence and objectives

- Quarterly cycle: goal-setting at cycle start, mid-cycle check-in at 45 days, end-of-cycle review and rating. Align team goals to company OKRs.
- Annual calibration: People Ops and leadership conduct level and compensation calibration once per fiscal year.

Ratings and calibration

- Use a three-tier rating (Meets Expectations | Exceeds Expectations | Needs Development) linked to behavioral anchors. Managers provide written summaries and evidence for ratings.
- Calibration committee reviews manager ratings for consistency. Any rating change after calibration must be documented with rationale.

Feedback best practices

- Managers should: give timely feedback (within 48 hours of observation), balance positive/constructive comments, use examples, and document significant feedback in the HRIS note field.
- Peer feedback: encouraged through our internal feedback form; used as supplemental evidence in reviews.

Career conversations and growth plans

- Managers run career conversations at least twice per year. Document agreed milestones and skills required for the next level. People Ops maintains level descriptions and promotion criteria.

Manager playbook: 1:1s, coaching, and performance conversations

- 1:1 cadence: weekly for new direct reports (first 3 months), minimum biweekly thereafter. Always include an agenda shared in advance.
- Coaching: use the GROW model (Goal, Reality, Options, Will) for development-focused conversations.
- Difficult conversations and performance improvement plans (PIPs): consult People Ops before initiating a PIP. PIPs should be time-boxed (30-90 days), include measurable success criteria, regular manager check-ins, and People Ops oversight.

Policies & compliance highlights

- Background checks: required for all staff; contingent offers are sent after a successful background check (exceptions must be approved by People Ops + Legal).
- Eligibility to work: hiring requires documentation per country (immigration cases handled by People Ops + Legal).
- Confidential information and IP assignment: all hires sign the standard employment agreement and IP assignment prior to contribution.

Checklists and templates

- Role Intake form (link in HRIS)
- Phone screen template (recruiter)
- Interviewer scorecard template
- Offer letter template
- 30/60/90 plan template
- Onboarding buddy checklist

Template example: Interviewer scorecard (text)

Competency | Description | 1 (Low) | 3 (Bar) | 5 (High)
---|---|---:|---:|---: 
Technical mastery | Knowledge of system design and coding patterns relevant to role | Superficial understanding; major gaps | Solid architecture & implementation skills for IC level | Deep subject matter expert; mentors others
Collaboration | Works with cross-functional partners effectively | Frequently unclear or unavailable | Reliable collaborator who communicates proactively | Drives cross-team alignment and influence

Escalation & support

- For equity or compensation exceptions, escalate to Senior People Ops and Head of Talent.
- For legal questions (immigration, contractor classification), escalate to Legal.
- For workplace conduct or investigations, follow Security & Compliance incident response playbook and notify People Ops immediately.

Metrics & continuous improvement

People Ops will track and report the following quarterly metrics to leadership: time-to-offer, acceptance rate, new-hire retention 90-day, new-hire ramp time to proficiency, and manager satisfaction with onboarding (survey). Use these metrics to iterate on the playbook.

Appendices

A. Links and resources
- HRIS: Role intake, offer templates, onboarding tracker
- Learning & Development: recommended training catalog
- Legal: employment agreement templates and policy library

B. Frequently asked questions
- What is the standard notice period we expect? Typically 4 weeks for senior ICs; see individual employment agreements.
- Who approves remote work exceptions? Manager + People Ops + manager's manager for cross-region hires.
